title: The Tuesday Club
description: Walk through 1890s Chicago as Rosa and follow one girls' club at Hull House from its first meeting to its goodbye. The game pauses three times for group activities.
players: Groups of 4, one phone per pair
concept: Social group work: what makes a group, stages of group development, social goals model

title: Term Duel
description: Rock-paper-scissors your way around the room: win and name a term, lose and explain it. Tick off every term on your own phone.
concept: Course vocabulary: What Makes a Group; Group Stages & Social Goals; Community Work

title: Storm Over Clear Creek
description: You doze off in a hard English lecture, a typhoon cuts the power, and you wake up in a mountain village. Watch the need-based path fail, discuss, then rewind and guide the social worker down the asset-based path. Pick the wrong response and it's Game Over. Needs a password from your teacher.
players: Played in class: solo on a phone, a pair on one phone, or a pair on the projector with an 8BitDo
concept: Community work: NBCD vs. ABCD, cycle of dependency, community principles, Rothman's three models, PARK, practice steps

title: Key Term Tycoon
description: A board game for the projector: teams roll the dice, explain key terms to buy them, answer questions to dodge rent, and draw Pop Quiz cards built from the exam's question types. The richest team wins. Needs a password from your teacher.
players: Played in class on the projector: up to 4 teams, one 8BitDo passed between team volunteers
concept: Midterm review: key terms from the study sheet and the six exam question types

title: Which Hat?
description: Meet the four hats a supervisor wears, then role-play in groups of four: the supervisor opens, the worker reads a real-life problem, and the two observers decide which hats were used before the roles switch. Four rounds, so everyone supervises once.
players: Groups of 4, one phone or tablet per group
concept: Social work supervision: the four functions (educational, administrative, supportive, mediating)

title: The Family Next Door
description: Five days, six good ideas, and every one is a guess. Learn research, pass card-sort BSW and MSW exams, then come home with 30 days to save the empty lot: interview, watch the lane at night, survey, check sources, and win the town hall with evidence.
players: Pairs on one phone: one taps, one reads aloud; decide exam answers together
concept: Social work research: ways of knowing and the halo effect, empirical research, five purposes, quantitative vs. qualitative, deductive vs. inductive, research questions and hypotheses, six steps, literature review, ethics, evidence-based practice, needs assessment, output vs. outcome, comparison groups

title: Safety Net Dispatch
description: Your group runs a city's safety-net dispatch center. Six experts each hold one strategy sheet, so the answers are spread around the circle. A short tutorial first, then every question is played in five steps: read, search, show, prove, approve. Match plan items to strategies, dispatch case reports, then answer like the licensing exam. Bilingual, about 37 minutes. Needs a password from your teacher.
players: Groups of 8, one tablet per group, plus a printed set of Expert Sheets and a Supervisor Card
concept: Social Safety Net 2.0 (強化社會安全網計畫2.0): core value, three family types, how a report travels, who's who, levels of prevention, new service groups, six strategies, exam-style answers
